public_rationale: The original manuscript supports the claim as a description of its headline results. Its best accuracy averaged across templates was 80.6%, and most tested model families showed little or no consistent benefit from greater size. The wording needs qualification: some prompt-specific scores exceeded 80.6%, and several families benefited from scaling. These results do not establish an enduring 80% ceiling.
limitations: Support depends on reading 80.6% as the overall mean, not the maximum across every prompt configuration.
The study tested a finite collection of model families and sizes.
Observed weak scaling in this experiment does not establish that future scaling cannot improve performance.

our_interpretation: The target is the 2022 Ruis et al. study as available when the post appeared, not subsequent models or paper revisions.
The ordinary reading of 80.6% is the paper's headline accuracy averaged across prompt templates, including its few-shot evaluations.
Scaling means increasing model size within the tested model families. 'Most models' is read as most families, since scaling requires comparisons between sizes.

Negligible means little or no consistent improvement across the sizes tested, judged against the paper's reported comparisons. This is not a claim that every family had a flat curve or that a permanent ceiling was proved.
The target period is the study's 2022 experimental results. The post does not specify individual experiment dates.
criteria.support_condition: The original manuscript reports a best overall mean accuracy of 80.6%, and its size comparisons show little or no consistent improvement for most tested model families.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The original manuscript reports a higher best overall mean accuracy under its main evaluation protocol, or substantial consistent gains with size for most tested model families.

evidence.locator: Section 4.2; see also Section 4.1, Figure 2 and Table 58
evidence.explanation: The best overall mean is 80.6% with 30 examples; Section 4.1 reports near-zero or decreasing slopes for many families, with only Cohere, T0 and InstructGPT-3 performing best at their largest tested size. The same source qualifies the headline: structured prompts average 81.7%, and Table 58 includes an individual-template score of 82.8%.
